title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 234 (Consequence of inducing agent or principal to act on belief as to exclusive liability)

content.overview: Section 234 provides that when a person who has made a contract with an agent induces the agent to act upon the belief that the principal only will be held liable, or induces the principal to act upon the belief that the agent only will be held liable, he cannot afterwards hold liable the agent or principal respectively.
content.glance: Induce belief of exclusive liability of principal or agent — cannot afterwards hold the other liable.
content.study: Where a person who has made a contract with an agent induces the agent to act on the belief that only the principal will be held liable, that person cannot afterwards hold the agent liable. Where that person induces the principal to act on the belief that only the agent will be held liable, that person cannot afterwards hold the principal liable. Current-law framing: identify the induced belief (principal-only or agent-only); apply the corresponding bar on holding the other party liable.

sections.heading: Induced belief — principal only liable
sections.body: If the person induces the agent to act on the belief that only the principal will be held liable, that person cannot afterwards hold the agent liable.

sections.heading: Induced belief — agent only liable
sections.body: If the person induces the principal to act on the belief that only the agent will be held liable, that person cannot afterwards hold the principal liable.

provisions.title: Consequence of inducing agent or principal to act on belief that principal or agent will be held exclusively liable

examples.title: Belief that only principal is liable
examples.body: A contracts with agent B and induces B to proceed on the basis that only principal C will be liable. A cannot afterwards sue B personally.

hypotheticals.question: Can a third party always sue both agent and principal?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not where the third party induced a belief of exclusive liability of one of them under section 234.

distinctions.title: Exclusive-liability inducement (s. 234) vs right against personally liable agent (s. 233)
distinctions.left: Bars holding the other after inducing exclusive-liability belief
distinctions.right: Right of person dealing with agent who is personally liable

misconceptions.trap: The third party can always elect freely between agent and principal regardless of representations.
misconceptions.correction: Section 234 bars holding the agent or principal after inducing a belief of exclusive liability of the other.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 234 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the induced belief (principal-only or agent-only). II. Apply the corresponding bar. III. Conclude who cannot be held liable.
